# Introduction

Differential accessibility analysis was performed using the [limma-voom pipeline](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29)[@law2014voom;@ritchie2015limma] to identify peaks that were differentially accessible between Asymptomatic and Healthy Controls.

```{r setup,include=F,echo=FALSE}
options(bitmapType='cairo')
```

```{r setup2,warning=F,include=F}
#Create directories for analysis
source("code/globalfun.R")
```

```{r read-in-sample-sheet}
sample.sheet<-readRDS("output/sample_sheet.valid.rds")
sample.sheet$group<-factor(sample.sheet$group.x)
sample.sheet$batch<-factor(sample.sheet$batch)
```

```{r set-filters,echo=TRUE}
#Filters used in the analysis
cpm.filt<-8 # minimum counts per million
FDR.cutoff <- 0.05 #FDR used in differential accessibility analysis
FC.cutoff <- 1.5 #Fold change used to filter differentially accessible peaks
enrich.pval <- 0.01 #P-value used to filter enriched pathways/temrs
```

```{r load-multiqc-data}
load("output/processed_data.RData")
```

# Read Summarisation

Summarisation of reads to peaks was performed using *featureCounts* [@liao2014featurecounts] a function from **Rsubread** [@liao2019r;@liao2013subread] within the NFCore/ATAC pipeline.

```{r bar-plot-number-of-features-assigned, fig.height=10,fig.width=12, fig.cap="featureCounts: Assignments", echo=F}
ggplot(fcounts.stats, aes(
  x = Sample, y = Reads,fill=Stats)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(title = "",
       x = "",
       y = "# Reads",
       fill= "Stats") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(Reads/1000000,2),"M")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 12 
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 12 
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.8)
  )
```

\FloatBarrier

## Annotation of Summarised Peak Counts

Summarised peak counts were annotated to the human genome (GRCh38) using the *annotatePeaks* function in **homer**[@heinz2010simple] and then used to generate a digital expression matrix for downstream analysis.

```{bash re-run-annotation, eval=F}
#Reannotate concensus peaks
source ~/.bashrc
workdir=$(realpath $(dirname $0)|xargs -n1 dirname)
annotatePeaks.pl ${workdir}/output/NFCore_ATACseq/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.bed  hg38 -cpu 6 > \
${workdir}/output/NFCore_ATACseq/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.annotatePeaks2.txt
```

```{r load-annotate-fcounts,eval=FALSE}
suppressMessages(library(org.Hs.eg.db))
fcounts <- read.table(
  "output/NFCore_ATACseq//bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt",
  sep = "\t",
  header = T
)
annotation.info <- read.delim(
  "output/NFCore_ATACseq//bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.annotatePeaks2.txt",
  sep = "\t",
  header = T
)
annotation.info$Annotation2 <- unlist(lapply(annotation.info$Annotation, 
    function(y) trimws(strsplit(y, "\\(")[[1]][1])))
colnames(annotation.info)[1] <- "PeakID"
dge <- DGEList(fcounts,
               annotation.columns = c("Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length"))
colnames(dge)<-gsub(".mLb.*","",colnames(dge))
dge<-dge[,gsub("_T1","",sample.sheet$sample)]
rownames(dge)<-dge$genes$Geneid
dge$genes <- cbind(dge$genes, annotation.info[match(dge$genes$Geneid, annotation.info$PeakID), -c(1:5)])
save(dge, file = "output/dge.RData")
```

```{r load-dge}
load("output/dge.RData")
```

```{r get-peak-annotation-distribution}
counts.dist <- dge$counts %>% as.data.frame %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = colnames(dge),
               names_to = "Sample",
               values_to = "counts")
```

```{r density-plot, fig.cap="Density plot showing the distribution of peak counts"}
plotDensities(dge, legend = "topright", args.lengend = list(cex = 0.2))
```

## Design matrix

The 'group' column from Table 1 was used to generate the design matrix for the linear model, which was then used to fit the model to the data. The design matrix includes information about the experimental conditions and any potential batch effects that need to be accounted for in the analysis.

```{r design-matrix-creation}
sample.sheet$group<-factor(sample.sheet$group)
design.matrix <- model.matrix( ~ 0+group+batch, sample.sheet)
design.matrix_no_batch<-model.matrix(~0+group,sample.sheet)
colnames(design.matrix) <- gsub("-", "_", gsub(
  "group|batch", "", colnames(design.matrix)))
colnames(design.matrix_no_batch) <- gsub("-", "_", gsub(
  "group", "", colnames(design.matrix_no_batch)))
min.samples <- min(colSums(design.matrix))
design.matrix
```



```{r}
groups<-unique(sample.sheet$group)
counts.cpms<-cpm(dge)
counts.fit<-lmFit(counts.cpms,design = design.matrix)$coefficients[,groups]
counts.fit_exp<-as.data.frame(counts.fit>0.5)
counts.fit_exp$Annotation<-dge$genes$Annotation2
counts.fit_exp <- counts.fit_exp %>% 
  pivot_longer(,cols=1:length(groups),names_to = "Sample",values_to="Status") %>% 
  group_by(Sample,Annotation) %>%
  summarise(
    Freq = sum(Status == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(counts.fit),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r, fig.height=12,fig.width=12,fig.cap="Pie Chart showing the number of peaks and their associated region for each group"}
pie.chart <- ggplot(counts.fit_exp, aes(x = "", y = Freq, fill = Annotation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",
           width = 1,
           color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~Sample)+
  coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = paste0(Annotation,"(",format(round(Freq*100,digits = 1),nsmall=1),"%)")),
                  position = position_stack(vjust = 0.50),
                  size = 8 / .pt) +
  labs(fill = "Annotation") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "#666666")
  )+Seurat::NoLegend()
ggsave(pie.chart,
       filename = paste0(plots.dir, "/Distribution-of-peaks-pie-chart-by-group.pdf"))
print(pie.chart)
```

## Sex-specific peak expression

The expression of peaks assocated with sex-specific genes, DDX3Y and XIST, was examined across samples to assess the accuracy of sample sex annotation. The expression levels of these genes were visualized in a bar plot, with samples grouped by their respective conditions. This analysis helps to confirm the expected expression patterns of sex-specific genes in male and female samples.

```{r get-cpm-sex-genes}
cpm.sex <- counts.cpms %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(dge$genes$Gene.Name %in% c("DDX3Y","XIST")) %>% 
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Peak") %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = colnames(dge),
               names_to = "Sample",
               values_to = "cpm") %>% 
  mutate(group =sample.sheet$group[match(Sample,sample.sheet$sample)],
         Gene=dge$genes[match(Peak,dge$genes$Geneid),"Gene.Name"])
```

```{r sex-gene-barplot}
ggplot(cpm.sex,aes(x=Sample,y=cpm,fill=group)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~Gene,scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "",
       y = "cpm") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 12 
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 12 
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```


# Differential peak analysis

To understand the differences in peak accessibility, the [limma-voom pipeline](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29)[@law2014voom;@ritchie2015limma] for differential analysis was used.

\FloatBarrier

## Peak filtering

Peaks were excluded from further analysis if they did not satisfy the following conditions:

\begin{itemize}
\item did not have a cpm count \>= `r cpm.filt` in at least `r min.samples` libraries
\end{itemize}

```{r check-gene-types}
is.pred <- grepl("^GM", dge$genes$Gene.Name)
is.not_validID <- is.na(dge$genes$Entrez.ID) | is.na(dge$genes$Gene.Name) ==
"NA"
is.standard_Chr <- dge$genes$Chr %in% paste0("chr", c(1:23,
"X"))
```

### Distribution of peak CPMs across samples

The distribution of peak expression (cpm) across samples is shown in the figure below. The dashed line represents the minimum cpm threshold used for filtering peaks.
```{r cpm-expression-violin,fig.height=8,fig.width=8, fig.cap="Distribution of peak expression (cpm) across samples"}
cpm.exp<-cpm(dge) %>% as.data.frame() %>% pivot_longer(cols = colnames(dge),
               names_to = "Sample",
               values_to = "cpm") %>% mutate(group = sample.sheet$group[match(Sample,sample.sheet$sample)])
ggplot(cpm.exp, aes(x = Sample, y = cpm, fill=group)) +
  geom_violin() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "",
       y = "cpm") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cpm.filt,
             color = "grey80",
             linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 12 
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 12 
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

```

```{r check-how-many-peaks-pass-filter}
is.expr <- rowSums(cpm(dge) >= cpm.filt) >= min.samples
table(is.expr)
keep.peaks<-!is.pred & !is.not_validID & is.standard_Chr &
is.expr
table(keep.peaks)
```

```{r save-dge-for-geo-submission}
#Save digital expression for GEO submission
geo.submission.dir<-"GEO_submission/"
if(!dir.exists(geo.submission.dir)){
  dir.create(geo.submission.dir, recursive = T)
}
saveRDS(dge, file = file.path(geo.submission.dir,"/ATACseq_raw_peak_counts_DGEList.rds"))
```

```{r}
#Perform filter
dgl.exp <- dge[keep.peaks, , keep.lib.size = FALSE]
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
cat("Number of peaks before filter:",format(nrow(dge),big.mark = ","),"\n")
cat("Number of peaks after filter:",format(nrow(dgl.exp),big.mark = ","),"\n")
```

## Voom transformation and normalisation

```{r}
norm.method<-"none"
```

The read counts were transformed using the *voom* [@law2014voom] function within **limma** [@ritchie2015limma] and then `r ifelse(norm.method=="none", "Library size",norm.method)` normalised as shown by the mean-variance trend estimated from the data in the plot below.

```{r voom-norm, fig.height=6,fig.width=12, fig.cap="Voom: Mean - Variance trend plot"}
par(cex.main = 0.8,
    cex.axis = 0.6,
    cex.lab = 0.7)
y <- voomWithQualityWeights(
  dgl.exp,
  design = design.matrix,
  plot = TRUE,
  normalize.method = norm.method,
)
```

\FloatBarrier

The distribution of peak expression (cpm) post normalisation is shown in the figure below. The boxplots represent the distribution of cpm values for each sample after applying the voom transformation and normalisation.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
}
```

## Contrast design

The following comparisons were made for each of the Histone markers;

```{r contrast-design}
contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(
    Asymptomatic_Stim.vs.Ustim=Asym_S-Asym_US,
    Stim_Asymptomatic.vs.Control=Asym_S-Control_S,
    Unstim_Asymptomatic.vs.Control=Asym_US-Control_US,
    Control_Stim.vs.Unstim=Control_S-Control_US,
    levels = colnames(design.matrix)
)
#contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(
#    Asymptomatic.vs.Control=Asym-Control,
#    levels = colnames(design.matrix)
#)
```

`r paste0("**",colnames(contrast.matrix),"**",collapse="\n")`

Peaks were called differentially accessible if they achieved a False Discovery Rate of `r FDR.cutoff`.

## Calling DA peaks 

empirical Bayes moderated t-statistics were used to assess differences in accessibility between conditions, and peaks were called differentially accessible if they achieved a False Discovery Rate of `r FDR.cutoff`.

```{r run-fitting-contrasts}
fit.contrast<-contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts = contrast.matrix)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit.contrast)
```

The table below shows the counts of differentially enriched peaks across each comparison made.

```{r}
dt.all <- decideTests(fit2, p.value = FDR.cutoff,method="global")
summary(dt.all)
```

## Volcano plots

The volcano plots below show the distribution of differentially accessible peaks in `r colnames(contrast.matrix)`.

```{r, fig.cap=paste0("Volcano plot of ",comps.interest), fig.width=8,fig.height=8}
lfc_cutoff <- log2(FC.cutoff)
top_n_labels <- 20
down.col <- "steelblue"
up.col <- "orange"
no.de_col <- "lightgray"
theme.extra <- theme(
  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
  legend.position = "right",
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
)

min.fdr <- ceiling(max(-log10(unlist(sapply(top.de,function(x) x$P.Value)))) + 2)
max.lfc <- ceiling(max(abs(fit2$coefficients[,-ncol(fit2$coefficients)]))) + 2
x_limits <- c(-max.lfc, max.lfc)
y_limits <- c(-0.5, min.fdr)
max_y <- min.fdr - 0.1
min_x <- -max.lfc + 0.2
max_x <- max.lfc - 0.2  
  
  
for(comp in comps.interest)
{
  top.df <- topTable(fit2, coef = comp, number = Inf)
  plot_data <- top.df %>%
    mutate(
      Expression = ifelse(as.numeric(dt.all[Geneid,comp])==1,"Up", 
                          ifelse(as.numeric(dt.all[Geneid,comp])==-1,"Down","Not Significant")),
      Expression = factor(Expression, levels = c("Not Significant", "Down", "Up"))
    ) %>%
    arrange(Expression) 
    top_up <- plot_data %>%
    filter(Expression == "Up") %>%
    arrange(P.Value) %>% 
    head(top_n_labels)
    top_down <- plot_data %>%
    filter(Expression == "Down") %>%
    arrange(P.Value) %>% 
    head(top_n_labels)
    
  top_genes <- bind_rows(top_up, top_down)
  num_up <- format(sum(plot_data$Expression == "Up", na.rm = TRUE), 
                   big.mark =",")
  num_down <- format(sum(plot_data$Expression == "Down", na.rm = TRUE), 
                     big.mark =",")
  volcano_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(
    x = logFC,
    y = -log10(P.Value),
    color = Expression
  )) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "Up" = up.col,
      "Down" = down.col,
      "Not Significant" = no.de_col 
    )) + # Add threshold lines
    # geom_vline(
    #   xintercept = c(-lfc_cutoff, lfc_cutoff),
    #   linetype = "dashed",
    #   color = "black",
    #   alpha = 0.5
    # ) +
    # geom_hline(
    #   yintercept = -log10(FDR.cutoff),
    #   linetype = "dashed",
    #   color = "black",
    #   alpha = 0.5
    # ) + # Text annotations for the total counts in the top corners
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = max_x,
      y = max_y,
      label = paste("Up:", num_up),
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 5,
      fontface = "bold",
      color = up.col
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = min_x,
      y = max_y,
      label = paste("Down:", num_down),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 5,
      fontface = "bold",
      color = down.col
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = x_limits, ylim = y_limits)
  
  for (lab in c("unlabelled", "labelled"))
  {
    if (lab == "labelled")
    {
      # Add non-overlapping labels for top genes
      ggsave.plt <- volcano_plot +
        geom_text_repel(
          data = top_genes,
          aes(label = Gene.Name),
          size = 3.5,
          box.padding = 0.5,
          point.padding = 0.3,
          max.overlaps = Inf,
          show.legend = FALSE,
          color = "black"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        labs(
          title = comp,
          #subtitle = paste0("Cutoffs: adj.p < ", pval_cutoff),
          x = expression("Log"[2] * " Fold Change"),
          y = expression("-Log"[10] * " (P-Value)"),
          color = "Status"
        ) + theme.extra
      print(ggsave.plt)
    }
    else
    {
      ggsave.plt <- volcano_plot + theme.extra
    }
    ggsave(
      ggsave.plt,
      file = paste0(
        plots.dir,
        "/Volcano_plots/",
        comp,
        "-",
        lab,
        ".pdf"
      ),
      height = 8,
      width = 8
    )
  }
}
```

# Pathway Enrichment Analysis

GO and KEGG pathway enrichment for genes associated with differentially accessible peaks was performed using functions implemented in **limma**. Note that the p-values indicated in the tables below are un-adjusted for multiple testing. This means that only enriched pathways with very small p-values should be considered.

```{r}
enrich.dir<-file.path(analysis.tables,"Pathway_enrichment_results")
if(!dir.exists(enrich.dir)) dir.create(enrich.dir)
suppressMessages(library(GO.db))
```

```{r,eval=F}
enrich.rst <- NULL
for (comp in colnames(dt.all))
{
  comp.go <- goana(
    fit2,
    coef = comp,
    species = "Hs",
    geneid = "Entrez.ID"
  )
  
  comp.ke <- kegga(
    fit2,
    coef = comp,
    species = "Hs",
    geneid = "Entrez.ID"
  )

  comp.ke <- topKEGG(comp.ke, number = 100,p.value = 0.05)
  
  comp.go <- list(
    "GO.Molecular Function" = topGO(
      comp.go,
      number = 100,
      ontology = "MF",p.value = 0.01
    ),
    "GO.Biological Process" = topGO(
      comp.go,
      number = 100,
      ontology = "BP",p.value = 0.01
    ),
    "GO.Cellular Component" = topGO(
      comp.go,
      number = 100,
      ontology = "CC",p.value = 0.01
    ),
    "KEGG" = comp.ke
  )
  openxlsx::write.xlsx(comp.go,
                       file = paste0(
  enrich.dir, "/", comp, "-pathway-enrichment.xlsx"))
  enrich.rst[[comp]] <- comp.go
}
saveRDS(enrich.rst, file = paste0(enrich.dir, "/Pathways_enrich.RDS"))
```

# Pathway Enrichment Analysis

GO and KEGG pathway enrichment for genes associated with differentially detected peaks was performed using functions implemented in **limma**. Note that the p-values indicated in the tables below are un-adjusted for multiple testing. This means that only enriched pathways with very small p-values should be considered.

```{r}
enrich.dir<-"docs/Pathway-enrichment/"
if(!dir.exists(enrich.dir)) dir.create(enrich.dir)
if(!dir.exists(enrich.dir)) dir.create(enrich.dir, recursive = TRUE)

suppressMessages({
  library(GO.db)
  library(limma)
  library(org.Hs.eg.db) # Annotation database for Human (use org.Mm.eg.db for Mouse)
  library(AnnotationDbi)
  library(openxlsx)
})
```

```{r,eval=F}
# Define species parameters
species_code <- "Hs"        # "Hs" for Human, "Mm" for Mouse
org_db       <- org.Hs.eg.db # Change to org.Mm.eg.db if working with Mouse
kegg_links <- limma::getGeneKEGGLinks(species = "hsa")
# Helper function to map genes to GO terms
add_go_genes <- function(go_df, de_genes, db = org_db) {
  if (is.null(go_df) || nrow(go_df) == 0) return(go_df)
  
  go_ids <- rownames(go_df)
  
  # Fetch GO to Entrez mapping
  go2eg <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
    db,
    keys = go_ids,
    column = "ENTREZID",
    keytype = "GOALL",
    multiVals = "list"
  )
  
  # Fetch Entrez to Symbol mapping
  eg2symbol <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
    db,
    keys = as.character(de_genes),
    column = "SYMBOL",
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    multiVals = "first"
  )
  
  # Extract overlapping genes for each GO term
  genes_col <- sapply(go_ids, function(id) {
    term_entrez <- go2eg[[id]]
    overlap <- intersect(as.character(de_genes), term_entrez)
    symbols <- eg2symbol[overlap]
    symbols <- symbols[!is.na(symbols)]
    paste(symbols, collapse = ", ")
  })
  
  go_df$Genes <- genes_col
  return(go_df)
}

# Helper function to map genes to KEGG pathways
add_kegg_genes <- function(kegg_df, de_genes, species = species_code, db = org_db) {
  if (is.null(kegg_df) || nrow(kegg_df) == 0) return(kegg_df)
  
  pw_ids <- rownames(kegg_df)
  
  eg2symbol <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
    db,
    keys = as.character(de_genes),
    column = "SYMBOL",
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    multiVals = "first"
  )
  
  genes_col <- sapply(pw_ids, function(id) {
    path_entrez <- kegg_links$GeneID[kegg_links$PathwayID == id]
    overlap <- intersect(as.character(de_genes), as.character(path_entrez))
    symbols <- eg2symbol[overlap]
    symbols <- symbols[!is.na(symbols)]
    paste(symbols, collapse = ", ")
  })
  
  kegg_df$Genes <- genes_col
  return(kegg_df)
}

# Main loop


enrich.rst <- sapply(names(top.de), function(comp) {
  
  x<-top.de[[comp]]
  sapply(c("up", "down"),function(DAR.dir) {
    if (DAR.dir == "up") {
      genes.DAR <- x[x$logFC > 0, "Entrez.ID"]
    } else {
      genes.DAR <- x[x$logFC < 0, "Entrez.ID"]
    }
    
    genes.DAR <- na.omit(genes.DAR)
    
    # Run GO and KEGG enrichment
    comp.go <- goana(de = genes.DAR, species = species_code)
    comp.ke <- kegga(de = genes.DAR, species = species_code)
    
    # Extract top results
    comp.ke_top <- topKEGG(comp.ke, number = 100, p.value = enrich.pval)
    
    go.mf <- topGO(comp.go,
                   number = 100,
                   ontology = "MF",
                   p.value = enrich.pval)
    go.bp <- topGO(comp.go,
                   number = 100,
                   ontology = "BP",
                   p.value = enrich.pval)
    go.cc <- topGO(comp.go,
                   number = 100,
                   ontology = "CC",
                   p.value = enrich.pval)
    
    # Append mapped gene symbols to each result table
    comp.go_list <- list(
      "GO.Molecular Function" = add_go_genes(go.mf, genes.DAR, db = org_db),
      "GO.Biological Process" = add_go_genes(go.bp, genes.DAR, db = org_db),
      "GO.Cellular Component" = add_go_genes(go.cc, genes.DAR, db = org_db),
      "KEGG"                  = add_kegg_genes(comp.ke_top, genes.DAR, 
                                               species = species_code, 
                                               db = org_db)
    )
    
    # Export to Excel
    openxlsx::write.xlsx(
      comp.go_list,
      file = paste0(
        enrich.dir,
        "/Pathway-enrichment-for-genes-with-DARs-",
        DAR.dir,
        "-in-",
        comp,
        ".xlsx"
      ),
      rowNames = TRUE
    )
    
    return(comp.go_list)
  },simplify = F,USE.NAMES = T)
},simplify = F,USE.NAMES = T)
saveRDS(enrich.rst, file = paste0(enrich.dir, "/Pathways_enrich.RDS"))
```

```{r, results='asis'}
for(n in names(enrich.rst))
{
  cat("\n")
  cat("## Enriched pathways for DARs in ",n,"\n")
  cat("\n")
  for(DAR_dir in names(enrich.rst[[n]]))
  {
    cat("### DARs",DAR_dir," in ",n,"\n")
    cat("\n")
    pathway_output <- lapply(names(enrich.rst[[n]][[DAR_dir]]), function(group_name) {
      dt.table<-enrich.rst[[n]][[DAR_dir]][[group_name]]
      if(length(dt.table)==0)
        next  
    tagList(
      h3(group_name),
      DT::datatable(
        dt.table,
        rownames = F,
        options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE),
        width = "100%",
        elementId = paste0("pathway-tbl-", n, "_", group_name)
      )
    )
    })
  }
  
  # Render all collected tag elements
  print(tagList(pathway_output))
  cat("\n")
}
```
